title: SR 1 over Wabash River | 2004 roadway reconstruction
source_note: Primary: 50-page existing-plans bundle, original 1933 arch details plus 2004 B-25747 roadway reconstruction. Pages 40-50 concern a separate pedestrian bridge and are not used for this model. 2026 general plan cross-checks the overall floor envelope.
assumptions: Exterior visualization reconstruction, not an as-built survey, load rating or validated FEM mesh.
No internal reinforcement, prestressing strands, embedded studs, weld beads or fabrication holes. Material colors are visualization choices.
Source pages mix historical removals and proposed work. Only the explicitly named design state is modeled; the separately stored later references do not alter that state.
Buried foundations are hidden by default. Unknown driven pile lengths, terrain and approach-road terminal systems are omitted.
Bearing contact checks verify constructed geometric attachment only; they do not establish surveyed bearing elevations or fabrication tolerances.
Arch intrados and variable ring thickness are approximate, not original setting-out. 21.946 m clear arch openings differ from pier-center distances and overall floor length.
The 2026 overlay and repair operations are not modeled. The 2004 decorative lighting details supplied by the City of Bluffton are not available in this package.

detail_coverage.detail: Four whole arch barrels, spandrel walls cut to the 2004 level 610 mm below the sidewalk soffit and closed to 13 mm joints at the spandrel pilasters, and hidden fill envelopes under the new slab. Exact original multi-radius curve and spring haunch thickness remain unresolved.

12.229 m roadway slab, 300 mm (top at original P.G. + 49 mm, 2 % crossfall, 30.48 m vertical curve at the Abutment 1 end) between the 12.7 mm longitudinal expansion joints; sidewalk castings with the 779 mm curb unit, 280 mm curbs, sidewalks falling 2 % to the roadway, 13.8 m clear roadway and 17.322 m out to out; 13 mm open joints at the pilasters; 80 typical and 10 pilaster concrete brackets (sheets 11-14). End-zone brackets (end brackets, B1-B3), plan flare and drains are not modelled.

915 mm rails with the sheet-18 section (380 mm cap and base, 290 mm stem, 19 mm recessed panels in the sheet-17 layout), 13 mm open joints to the pier pilasters and to the span side of the abutment pilasters, and 960 mm pilasters centred on the support lines at the arch-ring face, 75 mm inside the locally widened coping. Rail end flare, wing-end pilasters and pilaster caps are omitted. Separate pedestrian-bridge sheets 40-50 were excluded.
Three piers and two abutment envelopes. No foundation adequacy or current condition inferred.

Exact arch setting-out, end-zone sidewalk brackets (end brackets and B1-B3, sheets 13-14), the sheet 15-1 concrete end walls and gauge-well wall, sidewalk end flare, cutwaters, decorative lighting supplied by the city, gauge-well hardware, drainage outlets, rail end flare and approach details remain incomplete.

known_deviations.deviation: The 90 brackets in the spans and under the rail pilasters are modelled. Not modelled: the brackets of the four floor-end zones beyond the abutment pilasters, i.e. the concrete end brackets of sheet 14 (838 mm wide, 305 mm from the end of each sidewalk structure) and brackets B1, B2 and B3 of sheet 13 (381 mm wide, at the 1410 / 2172 mm chains of sheets 11-12). The sidewalk there is a plain 190 mm slab on the curb unit.
known_deviations.reason: The brackets are dimensioned, but they cannot be placed as drawn on the modelled end zones. Beyond the P.C. lines at the abutment pilasters the sidewalks, rails and end-floor wall faces flare on R 27 819 (Abutment 1, sheet 9) and R 22 504 / 24 265 (Abutment 5, sheet 10), and the bracket faces "follow curvature of Sidewalk" (sheets 13-14); the end brackets bear on the concrete end walls and gauge-well wall of sheet 15-1 under the wing-end rail pilasters of sheet 18. The model keeps straight sidewalks, rails and end-floor wall envelopes there and has none of those walls or pilasters, so the brackets would miss their drawn faces and supports by up to several hundred millimetres. Settling it needs an end-zone reconstruction from sheets 9-10, 15-1 and 18 (flared walk_*, parapet_*_0/_5, panels_*_0/_5 and endwall_*, the end and gauge-well walls, the wing-end pilasters), after which the sheet 13-14 brackets can be added.

known_deviations.deviation: Beside the 610 mm bracket stems the spandrel pilasters are cut to the general 610 mm wall-cut level under the curb unit, so their projection beyond the spandrel face shows a step about 0.61 m below the sidewalk soffit on either side of each pilaster bracket.

A section through the pilaster off the bracket centre line, or a survey of the existing pilasters, would settle it.
